messages:
Alex: FYI, detection cleared — we contained the lateral auth attempt at 08:12 UTC, blocked IP range, revoked compromised API key. Starting PIR post-actions thread. TL;DR: no data exfil, some privileged tokens used, root cause: leaked deploy token in external CI cache.
Sanjay: Good catch. I pushed an initial vuln triage doc to the incident ticket: https://redwood.inc/INT-4532 — includes IOCs and affected services. Suggest scope: rotate all deploy tokens + scan CI caches for tokens older than 30d.
Maya: Agree on rotate. For RBAC: we should tighten the deploy role to remove org-wide write — change to repo-scoped deploys and add MFA requirement for token issuance. I'll draft the policy changes.
Irene: KMS note: the compromised token had decrypt access to the staging key (kms-stg-01). Recommend immediate key rotation for staging and ensure key access is gated by IAM condition on resource tag 'env=staging'. Also enable key usage logging if not already.
sec-bot: Alert summary: detection name=anomalous-deploy-auth, severity=high, triggered=1762002600, encap: 3 events.
Alex: Action items we should capture now: 1) Token rotations (prod/staging/dev) 2) RBAC policy update + rollout plan 3) KMS key rotation + audit log enablement 4) CI cache purge sweep 5) Tabletop to validate runbook changes 6) Outreach comms draft for impacted teams. Assign owners?
Maya: Taking RBAC policy update + rollout. I'll put a PR in infra-policy repo and include migration steps (2 window options: staged canary or org-wide immediate). Prefer staged canary.
Sanjay: I'll own token rotations + CI sweep. Plan: script to rotate tokens and invalidate old ones (will use /internal/rotate-token v2). ETA EOD tomorrow. Need service owners list from Maya for repo-scoped tokens.
Irene: I'll do the KMS rotation and enable CloudAudit logs for all keys. One Q: do we rotate customer-managed keys too or only our internal service keys? Recommend internal first, then windows for customer keys after legal comms.
Jesse: I'll schedule a tabletop for Friday 14:00 UTC to walk through detection -> containment -> communications. Invite list: eng-oncall, devex, sec, customer-ops, legal. Prep: bring runbook changes and checklists.
Alex: Comms: keep it internal-first. Ops should notify impacted service owners; customer-facing comms only if we confirm any customer data access (currently no). Jesse, please draft a short internal post-incident note after tabletop.
ops-bot: Deploy note: paused all CI deploys for 2 hours following rotation. Will auto-unpause after successful canary runs.
Maya: Quick template for RBAC change: ```diff
- role: deploy
- perms: repo:write, org:read
+ role: deploy
+ perms: repo:write (scoped), org:read (readonly)
+ conditions: mfa=true, token_age<=30d
```
Sanjay: Also adding scan command to CI sweep: `grep -R --exclude-dir=.git "ghp_\|api_key\|token" /builds || true` — will centralize hits into INT-4532.
Irene: Logging checklist: 1) Ensure KMS Admin calls logged 2) Set retention 90d for key usage logs 3) Add alert for cross-region key usage.
Jesse: Tabletop prep tasks: update runbook, pre-populate roleplay persona cards, and confirm access to the staging key snapshot. I’ll attach materials in the calendar invite.
Alex: Great. Two open decisions: (A) immediate org-wide RBAC lock vs canary; (B) whether to force customers to rotate tokens (we think no). Put votes in thread.
Maya: +1 canary. Prefer minimal blast radius.
Sanjay: +1 canary but expedite rotation timeline to 24h.
Irene: +1 canary for RBAC, but start KMS rotation now.
Alex: OK consensus = canary rollout for RBAC, immediate KMS staging rotation, token rotations EOD tomorrow. I'll update the incident ticket with owners and deadlines. Anyone want to add post-incident backlog items?
Maya: Add: policy doc for token issuance lifecycle + automation to expire old tokens.
Sanjay: Add: CI caching hardening (cache encryption & token scrubber).
Irene: Add: KMS access review automation + quarterly audits.
Jesse: Add: tabletop cadence quarterly and a 6-month full-scale drill.
Alex: Thanks all. Closing loop: sec-bot will post this summary to #incidents and I'll link the PIR ticket. We can re-open if new findings come up. :thumbsup:
